name: Baha Buyang
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Li, Jinfang 1999. Buyang yu yanjiu [A Study of Buyang], 286-pp. grammar (Glottolog med ref 137029); also Li Jinfang 1996 phonology (10 pp.). Chinese monograph, not online.
earlier_scan.note: Tai-Kadai variety expected tonal; grammar not accessible so no statement read.

sources.citation: Li Jinfang & Luo Yongxian. 2010. The Buyang language of South China: grammatical notes, glossary, texts and translations. Pacific Linguistics 607. Canberra: ANU. xii+231 pp. (open access, CC BY-SA, hdl 1885/146755)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent anywhere (searched full text). Ch. 2 (pp. 9-14): 7 lexical tones; 'A number of prefixes are pronounced with the neutral tone, labelled as 0.. compare these structurally to the sesquisyllabic wordshape'; other prefixes alternate full tone ~ neutral tone; complex unanalysed tone sandhi; first syllables of compounds may lose final nasals/stops.

sources.citation: Li Jinfang & Luo Yongxian. 2006. Notes on Paha Buyang. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 29.1: 1-40.
sources.note: Sec. 2.1.3-2.1.4 (pp. 8-9): same content as the 2010 book (7 tones, neutral-tone prefixes, tone sandhi, CV(V)(C)T syllable). No stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Edmondson, Jerold A. [2002 draft] 'Kra or Kadai languages' = pre-publication draft of ch. in Diller, Edmondson & Luo (eds.) 2008, The Tai-Kadai Languages, London: Routledge.
sources.note: Second-hand (from Li 1999): 'Buyang words often reflect a sequi-syllabic structure with the first syllable being toneless.' About Buyang generally; no stress statement, nothing Paha-specific on prosody.

sources.citation: Ostapirat, Weera. 2000. Proto-Kra. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 23.1: 1-251.
sources.note: No text; scanned pp. 1-64 only (chs. 1-3). Paha (Yanglian) data are the author's own fieldwork, but chs. 1-3 contain no synchronic Paha phonology sketch and no stress remark; remaining 190 pp. (comparative reconstruction) not read.

sources.citation: Li Jinfang. 1998. Diachronic evolution of initial consonants in Buyang. Mon-Khmer Studies 28: 115-135.
sources.note: scanned; historical phonology of initials across Buyang dialects; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Li Jinfang. 1996. The sound system of Baha Buyang. Pan-Asiatic Linguistics: Proceedings of the 4th International Symposium on Language and Linguistics, 141-150. Salaya: Mahidol University.
sources.note: scanned (no text). Sec. 3 Tones, p. 150: 7 tones; 'Some prefixes are pronounced with a light tone 0.' No statement on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Liang Min 梁敏. 2004. 布央语 [The Buyang language]. In 云南特殊语言研究 [Studies of special languages of Yunnan], 1-19. Kunming: 云南民族出版社; also Liang Min 1990 'The Buyang language', Kadai: Discussions in Kadai and Southeast Asian linguistics 2: 13-21.
